stories.title: S&P 500 jumps 1.60% to 7,297.49 in the Black Friday half-day, capping a 5.6% week
stories.body: At the 1:00 PM close the S&P 500 was 7,297.49 (+114.71, +1.60%), the Nasdaq Composite 24,129.50 (+2.31%), the Nasdaq-100 26,726.39 (+2.61%) and the Dow 50,774.94 (+591.99, +1.18%) (JBizNews, STL.News); the Russell 2000 ended at 2,750.30 (+1.71%) (Yahoo Finance). For the week the S&P 500 rose 5.60%, the Dow 5.46% and the Nasdaq Composite 6.68% (JBizNews). All 11 sector ETFs rose, led by technology (+2.80%) (Current Logic). SPY closed at $728.32 (+1.62%), still below its 200-day average of about $730.98 (us-market-data).
stories.why: SPY's close sits just under its 200-day average after only a half-day of 1-hour candles; Monday's first full session of completed 1-hour closes shows whether that level is cleared or rejected.

stories.title: Tesla +5.22% to $400 and Amazon +3.96% on Black Friday; Apple trails
stories.body: Tesla closed at $400.00 (+5.22%) on unconfirmed SpaceX merger speculation and a reported acquisition filing for a German toolmaker (Current Logic); TipRanks cited a report that it is pushing to buy a German maker of humanoid-robot parts. Amazon ended at $254.12 (+3.96%) after Adobe data showed a record $7.1 billion of Thanksgiving-day online spending and Amazon stretched its deals to 12 days (TipRanks). Meta rose 3.13% to $628.96 on reported talks with Anthropic on data centers in Japan, while Apple (+0.83%) trailed as OpenAI filed trade-secret counterclaims (Current Logic).
stories.why: TSLA and AMZN made the biggest megacap moves of a half-day; with only a few completed 1-hour candles Friday, Monday's first full-session closes test whether the moves hold.

stories.title: Chip index +4.69%: Intel +5.38%, AMD +4.56%, Broadcom +3.82%, while Nvidia lags at +0.80%
stories.body: The PHLX Semiconductor index closed at 9,186.71 (+4.69%) (JBizNews). Intel ended at $57.40 (+5.38%), AMD $424.54 (+4.56%) despite an Erste Group valuation downgrade, Broadcom $312.34 (+3.82%) and Nvidia $150.49 (+0.80%) (us-market-data, Current Logic). Nvidia trailed with export questions still open and a report that chip sellers won't supply Nvidia chips if capacity is loaned to Chinese companies (Current Logic); Trading Economics also cited a report about Blackwell chips reaching a Shanghai data center. No Intel-specific reason was found.
stories.why: Chips bounced hard, but NVDA's weak relative close shows the group is not moving as one; each name's own completed 1-hour closes matter more than the index.

stories.title: Banks and energy join the rally: JPMorgan +1.96%, Exxon +1.33% even as crude slips
stories.body: JPMorgan closed at $322.96 (+1.96%), Bank of America $49.07 (+1.09%), Exxon Mobil $160.18 (+1.33%) and Chevron $212.45 (+0.71%) (us-market-data). JPMorgan was named among the advancing groups (Reuters via STL.News); the financials ETF rose 1.15% and the energy ETF 1.26% (Market Indicators) even as WTI settled 0.7% lower at $83.08 (Reuters via AOL).
stories.why: XOM and CVX rose while crude fell, so the energy names are not simply tracking oil; banks rose with the 10-year yield near 4.94%.

stories.title: Micron +7.60% to $646.95 as memory stocks rebound after a near-40% monthly slide
stories.body: Micron closed at $646.95 (+7.60%) (us-market-data, Current Logic). Investing.com said it had shed nearly 40% over the prior month on memory-oversupply fears and weaker NAND prices; Current Logic tied Friday's move to the chip rebound and tight 2027 memory supply, as SanDisk jumped 15.96% on a Kioxia test on Nvidia hardware. TrendForce said conventional DRAM prices may keep rising through 2027 at a slower pace (TipRanks). Micron's buyback window opens Dec. 9 and it reports fiscal Q1 2027 results Dec. 17 (Investing.com).
stories.why: A bounce from oversold levels can retrace quickly; the first completed 1-hour closes Monday show whether buyers defend Friday's range.

stories.title: Silver +5.3% and gold +2.5% late Friday on bargain buying and Chinese demand
stories.body: Spot gold was near $3,653.00 (+2.45%) and spot silver near $43.62 (+5.32%) at 4:46 PM ET, Kitco said, citing the tech-led equity rally, improved risk appetite and renewed Chinese physical demand despite rising yields and a firmer dollar. February gold futures were at $3,671.30 (+2.31%) at 2:38 PM ET (Cestrian). GLD closed at $334.40 (+2.12%) and SLV at $39.40 (+6.20%) (us-market-data, Structure One feed).
stories.why: Metals rose despite higher yields; SLV's 6% half-day move leaves a wide 1-hour range, and futures trade again before Monday's open.

stories.title: Brent settles 1.2% lower but logs about a 3% weekly gain on Gulf supply attacks; OPEC+ meets Sunday
stories.body: WTI settled at $83.08, down 60 cents (0.7%), and Brent fell $1.13 (1.2%) to $95.44 after touching its highest since Nov. 9; for the week Brent rose about 3% and WTI fell 0.9% (Reuters via AOL). Reuters cited attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on Saudi facilities; The National said a strike temporarily disrupted Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, which the kingdom blamed on the Houthis, and that Ras Tanura also came under attack this week. OPEC+ is set to keep Q1 2027 output targets unchanged at Sunday's meeting, sources told Reuters. USO closed at $137.77 (−1.52%) and OXY at $54.17 (+0.41%).
stories.why: The OPEC+ decision lands on Sunday, after Friday's last completed 1-hour close; USO and OXY can gap Monday on the outcome.

stories.title: VIX falls 11.16% to 23.81, down about a third on the week
stories.body: The VIX closed at 23.81, down 2.99 points (−11.16%) from 26.80 (Cboe); it touched 27.52 during the session (Current Logic). Cestrian put it down 33.68% on the week, with the MOVE bond-volatility index at 95.29 (−2.32%) at 3:07 PM ET.
stories.why: Implied volatility is easing but still well above calm-market levels, so option premiums remain relatively expensive heading into the jobs report and the Fed meeting.

stories.title: 10-year yield rises 9 bp to 4.94% as futures keep pricing a December hike
stories.body: The 10-year Treasury yield ended at 4.94% (+9 bp), the 2-year at 4.69% (+8 bp) and the 30-year at 5.33% (+9 bp), with the dollar index at 104.04 (+0.36%) at 4:14 PM ET (Current Logic); Kitco put Wednesday's 10-year close at 4.845%. Futures assessments cited by Kitco put the chance of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 8–9 Fed meeting at about 96%.
stories.why: Stocks rallied while yields rose; if yields keep climbing toward 5%, rate-sensitive names can lag the index in the 1-hour closes.

stories.title: Asia surges on the chip rebound and Beijing support; Europe closes higher
stories.body: The KOSPI closed at 4,915.68 (+4.34%), the Shanghai Composite at 3,606.49 (+3.73%) after a rare midday State Council pledge to support equities, the Nikkei 225 at 58,711.11 (+2.11%) as AI sentiment recovered, and the Hang Seng at 22,694.77 (+2.11%) with the Hang Seng Tech index up 6.5% (Trading Economics). In Europe the DAX rose 0.87% to 25,434, the FTSE 100 0.85% to 10,700 as miners led, and the CAC 40 0.64% to 8,161 (Trading Economics).
stories.why: Overseas chip and policy strength lined up with the US rebound; Asia's Monday session is the first read on whether it carries into next week.

stories.title: October goods trade deficit widens to $149.5B vs $133.1B expected
stories.body: The advance goods trade deficit was $149.5 billion in October vs $133.1 billion expected and $135.1 billion in September, as imports jumped 6.1% to $365.3 billion. Wholesale inventories rose 0.9% vs 0.5% expected, and retail inventories rose 0.8% (ActionForex). Earlier in the week October core PCE inflation came in at 3.3% vs 3.2% expected and Q3 GDP at 4.3% annualized (Current Logic).
stories.why: A wider deficit subtracts from GDP estimates; with a December hike almost fully priced, the data matter more for yields than for stocks.

stories.title: S&P 500's 114.71-point gain topped the ~98-point move options priced; big SPY and QQQ call trades for Monday
stories.body: At Wednesday's close options priced about a 1.37% (98.40-point) move for Friday's S&P 500 expiry, centred near 7,185, with the week's priced range topping out at 7,183.79; Nvidia's IV rank was 92.2, the highest of the large names (Saxo). The index closed at 7,297.49 (JBizNews), above both. Current Logic's flow scan showed SPY Nov. 30 $725 calls ($20.2M notional), QQQ Nov. 30 $645 calls ($17.6M), and AMD call lines totaling about $23.3M in premium plus Dec. 18 $460 puts ($8.5M), without showing whether they were bought or sold.
stories.why: A move beyond the priced range means short-premium positions lost on the expiry; next week's contracts start from a higher base with implied volatility still elevated.

stories.title: Ahead: OPEC+ Sunday, ISM Tuesday, jobs report Dec. 4, then the Fed and Broadcom on Dec. 9
stories.body: OPEC+ meets Sunday (Reuters via AOL). Monday brings the Chicago PMI at 9:45 AM (prior 55.3) and the Dallas Fed survey (Investing.com). Tuesday has ISM manufacturing (consensus 55.2) and JOLTS, Wednesday ADP (consensus 80,000), Thursday ISM services (54.5) and Friday, Dec. 4, November payrolls (consensus 90,000, unemployment 4.1%) (CalculatedRisk). Jensen Huang's transcribed House interview is set for Dec. 1 (Current Logic). The Fed meets Dec. 8–9 (Kitco); Broadcom reports Dec. 9 after the close (Broadcom IR); Micron's buyback window opens Dec. 9 and it reports Dec. 17 (Investing.com).
stories.why: Weekend events (OPEC+) land after Friday's last completed 1-hour close, and the Dec. 4 jobs report is the main scheduled data before the Fed.
